From the coordinator session_01RAN5eniJPZwnDgHRYfWFQb, relayed by ROOT. After the p3dev-l1 deploy and walk, enter the walk's findings as found-work entries. (1) Take PR 47 in as a bundler job: `job start <bundler module id> --take-in 47`. Drop the workflow edit; the take-in refuses files outside the module's paths, so leave the deploy-test.yml change out of the job's branch. In the same job's task, add a product script that gathers every member's built dist output into one directory, for the development release's release.assemble and release.out. bundles.mjs today rebuilds stale bundles in place across eight dist directories, and the job also rebuilds the stale agent-worker and bio-plane bundles. (2) When that job merges, open a plain PR into the tranche that adds the deploy block (process3 PR 59) and the release block (assemble, out, checks; process3 dev release) to process/config.json, so `p3 deploy dev` and `p3 release dev` run. Then cut the first development release with `p3 release dev`: a draft only, no public release. (3) Keep running next work as status lists it. If a layer's modules sit under 'split or consolidate before its job', the split is next work: run it as jobs. Send reports to ROOT as usual.

URGENT, from the coordinator session_01RAN5eniJPZwnDgHRYfWFQb, relayed by ROOT: status now lists 44 modules from layers 1 to 11 as next work, each only because of the provider notice jurisdictions R119 (PR 40). The list is headed 'next work, layer 3', which is wrong. (a) Start no job whose only work is that notice, and no job for a module outside the open layer. (b) A process3 build is adding a notice triage: one read-only worker judges each user module affected or not, with file:line evidence; only the affected ones become jobs, the rest are recorded as answered. It comes with a pin move. (c) Until then, run only open-layer work with unmet marks of its own (today mail-door, layer 3), plus the deploy, walk, PR 47 take-in and release steps already sent. (d) Layer 2 closed implicitly: its 8 modules have 0 unmet marks. That is correct; no act is owed for it.
